title: Together, lives on
hook: an old couple, Nakula's parents, wish to meet again in future lives: shared faith, virtue, giving, wisdom

segments.voice: Yesterday: the firebrand from the pyre, and your line, for self and others. Did you manage one of each? Today, two people who did their practice side by side for a lifetime. Day six hundred sixty-four.

These two are not monks or nuns. They're an old married couple from the Bhagga country, known in the texts as Nakula's father and Nakula's mother. They were married young. One day they come to the Buddha together, and the husband says something remarkable for any marriage, ancient or modern. Since she was brought to me as a girl, he says, I don't know of ever having been unfaithful to her, not even in thought. And his wife says the same of him. Then they ask for something bigger. Today: together, lives on.
screen: `AN OLD MARRIED COUPLE.` → `MARRIED YOUNG.` → `NOT EVEN IN THOUGHT.`

segments.voice: Their request is simple and huge. We want to see each other not only in this life, but in lives to come. Is there a way? In the Buddhist picture, life doesn't end at one death, and beings are carried from life to life by what they've done and become. So the couple's question is a real one. And the Buddha takes it seriously. Yes, he says. If a husband and wife both wish to see each other in this life and the next, let them be equal in four things. Equal in faith, the trust that sets you on the path. Equal in virtue, the way you keep your conduct. Equal in generosity, the open hand. Equal in wisdom, seeing how things really are. If those four are shared, he says, they will see each other in this life and in the life to come. Notice what's not on the list. Not looks, not money, not even shared tastes in food. The bond he points to is a shared practice, two people walking the same way at the same pace. And it's a list you can actually work on together. Elsewhere in the Numbered Sayings, the Buddha names Nakula's father and mother as foremost among his lay followers in one quality: trust, the kind of closeness people can lean on. An honor shared by a husband and wife, and a happy marriage held up as a model.
screen: `MEET AGAIN IN LIVES TO COME.` · `SAME FAITH, SAME VIRTUE.` · `SAME GIVING, SAME WISDOM.` · then, large: `TOGETHER, LIVES ON.`

segments.voice: Sit for a few breaths and bring to mind someone close: a partner, a parent, a friend, a sibling. Picture their face. Now go through the four, gently. Is there something you both trust in? A way of behaving you both care about? A way you both like to give? Something you've both come to understand? Pick one. Think of a small way to do it together this week: a walk, a meal shared out, a quiet ten minutes side by side. The bell holds the time.
Together. Nakula's parents, the old couple of the Numbered Sayings, and the four things the Buddha said keep two lives side by side: faith, virtue, giving and wisdom, shared. Today's word.
Your line: side by side. Today, ask someone you love to do one small good thing with you, and do it side by side. Day six hundred sixty-four.

howItsDone: Buddhist teachers draw on the story of Nakula's parents in talks on marriage, and some Buddhist couples practice together by keeping the precepts, giving, and going to the temple as a family.

fork.setup: an old couple asks: how can we see each other again in lives to come? what does the Buddha say?
options: it can't be done; let go of each other.
be equal in faith, virtue, generosity and wisdom.

fork.reveal: he gives them four things to share. the answer isn't a vow or a farewell, but a practice they can do together.

original.note: Pali samasaddha: 'of the same faith,' the first of four; the sutta goes on: same virtue, same giving, same wisdom.

trapdoor: what you thought: Buddhism is mostly about leaving your family behind.
what it means: the Buddha told a married couple how to stay together, even across lives.
what a scholar hears: the sutta's name, samajivina, means 'living in harmony,' and the four 'sames' are its formula.

notes: AN 4.55 paraphrased. Confirm the setting (Bhagga country, Sumsumaragira, Bhesakala grove) and that both spouses make the faithfulness statement.
